name: Fort Bragg
tagline: Home of the airborne and special operations forces, near Fayetteville in the North Carolina Sandhills.
_note: Marquee Army post (Sandhills, NC). Name history: Fort Bragg -> Fort Liberty (June 2023) -> Fort Bragg (Feb 2025, now honoring WWII Pfc. Roland L. Bragg, not the Confederate general). Facts verified from official sources (home.army.mil/bragg, womack.tricare.mil, fortbragghousing.com, DeCA/AAFES, Wikipedia for corroborated headline facts). BAH MHA NC182 (Fort Bragg/Pope) via the bah_rates single source of truth. Housing operated by Corvias. Corrected 2026-11-09 from the website-page research (Base Guides/page-builder/research/bragg-facts.md): FORSCOM became U.S. Army Western Hemisphere Command at Fort Bragg on 2025-12-05; the All American Gate closed 2026-07-27 for up to 24 months; Housing Services Office (910) 396-1022; DoDEA on post is pre-K to grade 8 (high school E.E. Smith, Overhills for Linden Oaks); NC DPI 2025-26 school results; Longleaf Pine REALTORS prices; drive times are OSRM routing estimates with no traffic to Womack. Removed unverified superlatives ("largest"/"most populous" installation, "one of the biggest" housing inventories). Medium-confidence flags: base coords (approx), representative off-base ZIP 28314 (Fayetteville).

sections.title: Mission & Identity
data: Fort Bragg is the home of the airborne and special operations forces. It hosts the XVIII Airborne Corps, the 82nd Airborne Division, and U.S. Army Special Operations Command (USASOC).

It is also home to U.S. Army Western Hemisphere Command, formed at Fort Bragg in December 2025 from Forces Command (FORSCOM), Army North and Army South, and to the Army Reserve Command. The post carried the name Fort Liberty from 2023 to 2025 before being renamed Fort Bragg, now honoring Pfc. Roland L. Bragg, a World War II paratrooper who received the Silver Star.

sections.title: A High-Tempo Post: Where to Land Around Fayetteville

data.subtitle: Fort Bragg is huge and deployment-heavy, especially the rapid-response 82nd Airborne. Where you live around Fayetteville is the main decision, and proximity and a strong support network matter more here than at a quiet post.
intro: This is a fast-paced, deeply military community. The 82nd keeps a brigade on short-notice readiness, so deployments and field time are a way of life, and many families prioritize living close to the unit and to other military families.

The post touches Cumberland, Hoke, Harnett and Moore counties, and the county you live in sets your schools, your property tax and your commute. Since July 2026 the main All American Gate has been closed for road work, so drives from Fayetteville and Hope Mills take longer than they used to.

recommendations.advice: Spring Lake is about 13 minutes from main post with no traffic. Fayetteville and Hope Mills were 22 and 27 minutes through the All American Gate, so allow more while it is closed.
Median sale prices, January to September 2026: Fayetteville $247,000, Hope Mills $263,250, Raeford $295,000 (Longleaf Pine REALTORS).
Moore County (Southern Pines, Pinehurst) had 13 of 23 schools rated A or B in 2025-26, with the highest prices and a 43 to 53 minute drive with no traffic.
Combined property tax in Cumberland County runs from 0.699 per $100 of value outside towns to 1.29 in Spring Lake. Check it for the exact address.
Corvias runs on-post family housing, and living on post opens the DoDEA schools for pre-K through grade 8.

source.label: Garrison PAO (DVIDS); Longleaf Pine REALTORS; NC DPI; Cumberland County Tax

sections.title: Gates & Access
data: The All American Gate closed on July 27, 2026, for up to 24 months while the All American Freeway is repaired and the Gruber Road bridge is replaced. Its visitor center stays open.
Open 24 hours: Canopy Lane, Long Street, Chicken Road, Yadkin, Honeycutt and R. Miller gates. Butner, Manchester and Rock Merritt keep limited hours, so check them before you rely on them.
Visitors without a DoD ID need a visitor pass and a REAL ID-compliant ID from the Visitor Control Center.
Gate hours and visitor requirements change, so confirm the current details on the official Fort Bragg site before you go.

source.label: Fort Bragg Garrison PAO via DVIDS, July 28, 2026

sections.title: On-Base Housing
data: On-post family housing is privatized and run by Corvias, with neighborhood centers at Corregidor, Casablanca, Ste. Mere Eglise, Nijmegen, Hammond Hills, Ardennes/Pope/Bataan, Normandy/Bastogne Gables, Linden Oaks and Randolph Pointe.

Ask Corvias or the Housing Services Office how to apply and what the current wait is: (910) 396-1022, Soldier Support Center, Building 4-2843 (basement), 7:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. on weekdays. Corvias work orders: (866) 206-1365.

source.label: DoD 2026 BAH Rates, MHA NC182 (Fort Bragg/Pope)

sections.title: Schools
data: Families who live on post can use the DoDEA schools there, which run from pre-K through grade 8. There is no DoDEA high school: on-post students are zoned for E.E. Smith High School, and Linden Oaks families for Overhills High School in Harnett County. From 2026-27, on-post students may choose another Cumberland County high school if it has space, but buses run only to E.E. Smith.

Off post, the county sets the district. In the 2025-26 state results, Cumberland County had 20 of 79 schools rated low-performing (down from 27), Hoke 5 of 13, Harnett 6 of 25, and Moore 2 of 23, with 13 Moore schools rated A or B.
Your assigned schools depend on your address, so confirm the district and campus with the School Liaison Office at (910) 432-1023.

source.label: Military OneSource Fort Bragg education; Fort Bragg School Liaison; NC DPI 2025-26 results

intro: Whether to rent or buy is the biggest money decision of most PCS moves, and the answer is mostly about how long you'll be here and how steady the local market is.
rent: Your tour is short (about two years or less) or your orders feel uncertain.
You want time to learn the area before committing to a neighborhood.
You'd rather not gamble on resale timing when you PCS out.
Your BAH comfortably covers rent in the areas you'd consider.
buy: You expect to be here three or more years.
You want to use your VA loan and build equity instead of paying rent.
The market is steady and you could rent the home out later if needed.
You've found a neighborhood and commute you're confident about.
data.bottom_line: There is no universal right answer. BAH is the same whichever town you live in, so lower prices and property tax leave more of it in your pocket. Run your BAH against the rent and home prices above, weigh your tour length and the deployment tempo, and talk to a lender and an agent who work with military families before you commit.

intro: The first month at a new duty station is mostly logistics. Knocking these out early makes everything else easier.

steps.title: Line up temporary lodging
steps.text: Book on-base lodging or a short-term rental before you arrive. You can claim Temporary Lodging Expense (TLE) for a limited number of days while you house-hunt.

steps.title: In-process and update DEERS
steps.text: Report to your unit and finance, and make sure DEERS and ID cards are current for every family member so TRICARE and base access work.

steps.title: Start with the Housing Office
steps.text: Check on-base availability and get the housing office's read on off-base neighborhoods before you sign anything.

steps.title: Register your vehicle and sort access
steps.text: Handle base access and vehicle registration, and learn the visitor-pass process for guests. Bring your registration and insurance.

steps.title: Enroll the kids in school
steps.text: Contact the gaining school district or DoDEA early and bring records and immunizations. The School Liaison Office can help with the transfer.

steps.title: Set up healthcare
steps.text: Update your TRICARE region and enrollment so you can be seen at Womack Army Medical Center or network providers.

data.q: Is it Fort Bragg or Fort Liberty?
data.a: Fort Bragg. It was renamed Fort Liberty in 2023, then renamed Fort Bragg in 2025, this time honoring Pfc. Roland L. Bragg, a World War II paratrooper, rather than the Confederate general.
Yes. The All American Gate closed on July 27, 2026, for up to 24 months. Canopy Lane, Long Street, Chicken Road, Yadkin, Honeycutt and R. Miller gates are open 24 hours.

It's the home of the airborne and special operations forces: the XVIII Airborne Corps, the 82nd Airborne Division, and Army Special Operations Command, plus Army Western Hemisphere Command (formerly FORSCOM) and the Army Reserve Command.

Spring Lake is closest, Fayetteville and Hope Mills have the most homes at the lowest prices, Raeford and Harnett County are in between, and Southern Pines and Pinehurst have strong schools at a longer commute and higher prices. On-post housing is run by Corvias.
Fort Bragg is MHA NC182 (Fort Bragg/Pope). Use the calculator above for your grade.
